## crank-mem (project memory)

This project keeps a code graph in `.crank/code.db` and project memory in `.crank/cerebrum.md`.

- `crank-mem anatomy [<dir>]` lists the project's 25 file(s) with descriptions, token sizes and symbol line ranges (symbols for 25 files are still being parsed); use it before slice-reading a large file.
- Code: `crank-mem outline <file>` lists a source file's symbols with line ranges, and `crank-mem unfold <file> <symbol|line>` prints one in full. `crank-mem callers|callees <symbol>` and `crank-mem impact <file|symbol>` show what calls what and what a change reaches.
- Memory is not proof of current behavior; verify a consequential claim
  against the cited file before relying on it.
- ADR protocol: decisions that are hard to reverse, surprising, AND carry a
  real trade-off get an ADR (`NNNN-slug.md`, Pocock style) in the ADR
  directory. Existing ADRs are settled — don't relitigate them.
